facts.t: An Indian MLA's vote is worth more in Uttar Pradesh than in Sikkim
facts.d: The value of an MLA's vote is the state's population divided by the number of MLAs, divided again by a thousand. A UP legislator's vote is worth over two hundred; a Sikkim legislator's, seven. Federal weighting written directly into arithmetic.

facts.t: India's President can be re-elected indefinitely
facts.d: There is no term limit in Articles 54 to 59. The American two-term cap came only with the 22nd Amendment in 1951, after Franklin Roosevelt won four times — before that it was merely a convention set by Washington.

facts.t: India's pocket veto has no clock
facts.d: The American pocket veto operates on a ten-day rule. Article 111 sets no time limit at all, which is how President Zail Singh sat indefinitely on the Indian Post Office (Amendment) Bill in 1986 and killed it without ever refusing assent.

bank.q: The President of India is elected by:
o: Proportional representation by single transferable vote, through secret ballot
Simple majority of both Houses of Parliament
bank.e: Proportional representation by means of the single transferable vote, with a secret ballot, under Articles 54 and 55.

bank.q: With reference to the electoral college for the Indian President, consider the following statements:
s: It includes elected members of both Houses of Parliament.
It includes elected members of state legislative assemblies, and of Union Territories with legislatures.
It includes members nominated to the Rajya Sabha.
bank.e: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Nominated members are expressly excluded from the presidential electoral college.

bank.q: The value of an MLA's vote in the presidential election is calculated as:
o: State population divided by number of MLAs, divided by 1,000
Number of MLAs divided by state population, multiplied by 1,000
Total MLA vote value divided by number of MPs
bank.e: That is the MLA formula. An MP's vote value is the total value of all MLA votes divided by the number of elected MPs.

bank.q: Which one of the following is NOT correct about the two presidencies?
o: India's President is a nominal executive; America's is a real executive
India's President has no term limit; America's is capped at two terms
India's President is Supreme Commander in a ceremonial sense
bank.e: The American President has no ordinance power — only Congress legislates. Executive orders are a different instrument and are judicially reviewable.

bank.as: The American electoral college can produce a President who lost the popular vote.
bank.rs: Most states allocate their electors on a winner-takes-all basis.
bank.e: Both true and the Reason explains the Assertion. India's weighted system is designed for federal proportionality rather than popular mandate, so the question does not arise there.

bank.q: Match List I (feature) with List II (provision or figure):
pairs: A. Presidential election disputes in India
B. Electors needed to win in the United States
D. Impeachment of the Indian President
bank.e: Article 71 for disputes, 270 of 538 electors to win, fifty proposers and fifty seconders for nomination, and Article 61 for impeachment.

s: The Indian President must be qualified for election to the Lok Sabha.
The American President must be a natural-born citizen.
Both must be at least forty years of age.
bank.e: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Both offices require a minimum age of thirty-five, not forty.

bank.q: All of the following are powers of the President of India EXCEPT:
o: Exercising a line-item veto over money bills
bank.e: Neither India nor the United States has a line-item veto. India's President has a suspensive veto and an unlimited pocket veto.

bank.q: The American President's pocket veto operates on:
bank.e: Ten days, excluding Sundays, while Congress stands adjourned. India's pocket veto has no prescribed limit at all.

bank.q: With reference to discretion, consider the following statements:
s: The Indian President's discretion is very limited, arising mainly in a hung Parliament.
The American President has broad discretion, especially in foreign policy and military matters.
The Indian President exercises executive power independently of ministerial advice.
bank.e: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Article 74 binds the President to the aid and advice of the Council of Ministers.

bank.q: Droupadi Murmu became which President of India?
bank.e: The fifteenth, elected in 2022 under Articles 54 to 59 and the Presidential and Vice-Presidential Elections Act, 1952.
